RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Foster
Member ID: W276906709
Reference Number: POC-EED29F7594-68772
Requested Service: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
Date of Notice: 2026-08-11
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-07

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11 (Reference Number POC-EED29F7594-68772). The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

Governing guideline. Anthem/Carelon Medical Benefits Management applies the Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines for Musculoskeletal — "Joint Surgery" (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, Effective Date 11/15/2025), Knee Arthroplasty (Total/Partial/Revision Knee Replacement) section, to requests for this procedure. I have reviewed the portion of that guideline that is publicly posted. I was able to confirm the following general review framework, which I quote directly because it is text I actually retrieved from the guideline:

"Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention."

"The anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms, including from delay or decreased access to services that may result (net benefit)."

"Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent."

I was not able to obtain the exact, current wording of the specific "Clinical Indications" bullet points for the Knee Arthroplasty section (the compartment-specific radiographic and conservative-care thresholds that this determination appears to turn on). I am therefore not quoting or reconstructing that specific language here, and I have not attributed any such wording to the plan. I respectfully request that Anthem/Carelon (1) identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria within the Knee Arthroplasty section that the submitted imaging was found not to satisfy, and (2) apply the following clinical record to those specific, named criteria.

Clinical record supporting medical necessity:

1. Chronicity and severity of symptoms: Ms. Foster has had 14 months of progressive knee pain that is unrelieved by rest, consistent with an advanced, non-self-limiting degenerative process rather than an acute or transient condition.

2. Documented failure of conservative management:
   - Supervised physical therapy: 16 weeks (2026-02-25 through 2026-06-17), 24 completed visits, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of symptoms.
   - Pharmacologic treatment: NSAIDs trialed for 4 months with inadequate relief.
   - Corticosteroid injection administered 2026-03-26, yielding only 2 weeks of partial relief.
   This represents a comprehensive, multi-modality, well-documented course of non-operative treatment that did not achieve durable symptom control.

3. Objective imaging findings: MRI of the knee dated 2026-06-27 demonstrates full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes isolated to the medial compartment. This is direct radiographic/MRI evidence of advanced, single-compartment osteoarthritis — the compartment-limited pattern that partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, rather than total knee replacement, is specifically designed to address.

4. Functional impairment: Ms. Foster is unable to climb stairs without assistance and wakes 3-4 times nightly due to pain, reflecting a significant, ongoing impact on activities of daily living and sleep.

5. Examination findings: Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, corroborating the imaging findings with a consistent clinical exam.

6. Absence of contraindications: No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker — none of which are barriers to surgical candidacy.

7. Surgeon assessment: The requesting surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist (orthopedic surgery), has evaluated Ms. Foster and recommended partial knee replacement based on this history, examination, and imaging.

Taken together, this record documents (a) a confirmed diagnosis based on a complete history, physical examination, and diagnostic imaging; (b) a well-documented, multi-modality trial of conservative care that has failed to provide durable relief; and (c) objective, compartment-specific imaging findings of advanced degenerative disease. I therefore believe the request satisfies the general review framework quoted above, and I ask the plan to identify the specific Knee Arthroplasty criterion it believes is unmet so that this appeal, or a peer-to-peer discussion with Dr. Lindqvist, can directly address it.

Requested action:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 27446 for Ms. Foster.
2. If the denial is not fully reversed on this record, please arrange a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Lindqvist and the plan's/Carelon's physician reviewer before further action, and identify the specific criterion at issue in writing.
3. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the applicable internal appeal timeframe, and, if this appeal is not resolved in Ms. Foster's favor, please provide instructions for requesting an independent External Review through the Kentucky Department of Insurance.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-03-26)
- MRI report and images dated 2026-06-27
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist [attached/to follow]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the Notice (by 2027-02-07). Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the contact information above. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster
